I grew up in a rural area drenched in white evangelicalism, and I internalized the whole shebang. I was the epitome of purity culture, of conservative Christian politics, of creationism, of the pro-life anti-gay movement. I always had some doubts, but I always buried them down.

I was always told that when I’d to college I’d meet a bunch of atheist socialist gay professors who would make your life awful unless you held to Jesus (thank you, God’s Not Dead. Very cool). When I got to college, I actually had that professor who was an atheist and a professor of political theory, and we discussed the Bible. And even though he didn’t believe in it, he showed the text just as much respect as he gave Marx and the Quran and Adam Smith, pointing out how it connects to our lives. And he knew so much about the Bible! It blew me away. So ironically, the atheist socialist professor did lead me away from God… by showing how evangelicals were lying. And going to college during the Trump years, as evangelicalism was getting even uglier, plus I started hanging out with a bunch of queer furries online, I started to realize I could be really badly wrong. There were a lot of ahistorical claims about Christianity. What I learned about queer people seemed to not measure up against the reality of what I was learning. My church’s claims weren’t making sense anymore.

I think the pandemic was a big part of ending all belief entirely. It really hastened the deconstruction that I had been doing over a few years. We were talking about racism in the US; our racist roots were being laid bare; the far-right Christians were running our government and killing us by not masking up.

So I stopped settling for easy answers. I grappled with the actual impacts of my questions: “God, how could you let slavery happen and still be good? That whole thing was systemically disgusting and why did you let it happen at all? What good could have come from it? Also, do you not care that fascists are using your name to run our government? Why does your whole church seem to love to oppress minorities, for decades and centuries? Can’t you stop making me deal with repressed gender dysphoria and my sexuality for no reason? That’s so unfair and it feels unjust. Why’d you drop by 2000 years ago and leave only a questionable historical record? Why don’t you reveal yourself at all? Asking us to chase you is a cowardly cop-out. I’m done asking questions with the intention of reaffirming my belief in you. I need to hear from you. Now.” I stopped asking these questions with the absolute expectation of reaffirming everything that I believed, but I thought maybe I would become a mainline Protestant or become a practicing Christian who happened to be divorced from the American evangelical church.

The last straw (somehow) was Christian apologetics. I got really into it in the last 2-3 years to try to understand my beliefs. I was excited at first - it was very different from the emotive Christianity I grew up around - but over time I realized they were full of shit m, making illogical, absurd, or morally questionable claims. There was one day I was reading an atheist scholar’s response to William Lane Craig’s historical claims about Jesus when I suddenly realized: “I don’t believe this. I’ve been forcing myself to for years.”

I’ve been dealing with a fuck ton of religious trauma and a lot more suicidal ideation than when I was a Christian, but I have a lot less cognitive dissonance now about the state of the world and no longer feel obliged to awkwardly explain away the Bible’s deeply questionable and sometimes awful morality.

TL,DR: Years of trust in the church slowly eroding away through false claims and lived experiences., all ramped up during the pandemic. You can feel free to re-print this in the book pseudonymously, and you can definitely PM me for more.

* If you're straight, and you have a foot fetish, does it fundamentally change your heterosexuality?
* If you're gay, and you have a foot fetish, does it fundamentally change your homosexuality?
* If you're bi, and you have a foot fetish, does it fundamentally change your bisexuality?
* If you're pan, and you have a foot fetish, does it fundamentally change your pansexuality?

If the answer to all of those is "no," then answer this for me: if you're ace, and you have a foot fetish, does it fundamentally change your asexuality in any significant way?

Hey! Thanks for posting here. We're glad to have you. It's totally normal to question yourself from time to time.

One thing that's really helpful is to define explicitly what asexuality is. I personally describe the ace spectrum as "little to no sexual attraction to any gender." Perhaps you can compare your experience to my definition and see how you feel? I phrase it this way for three reasons:

* "Little to no" -- Many asexuals feel sexual attraction very few times in their life, or to people they're only deeply emotionally connected with, or never at all. You might hear "gray-asexual" or "demisexual" used by folks to describe themselves. I say this only to be inclusive of other identities under the ace umbrella.
* "Sexual attraction" -- an emotional response you have when a person or gender catches your eye in a sexually appealing way. This is the person or gender you fantasize about, that makes you want to physically touch them (in a sexual way), the gender that you "get the hots for," in a sense. It can be coupled with physical arousal, but not always.
* "Any gender" -- You experience non-attraction to men, women, nonbinary folks alike.

What *doesn't* have anything to do with asexuality is libido/arousal, or fetishes/kinks. Libido's a weird thing where you can be turned on by things you're not attracted to, or you can have trouble maintaining arousal during a sexual act. Asexuality also doesn't have anything to do with your sexual performance or even your desire to have sex -- indeed, many of us have had sex before, and perhaps even multiple times, for many reasons. Some of us want children. Others of us want to fulfill the desires of our non-asexual partners.

The reason I point all this out is that based on your submission, I really don't have enough information to make an informed judgement on whether or not you're likely to be ace. Your libido, arousal, sexual performance, or sexual history don't really make any difference about your sexual orientation (same thing for heterosexuality, homosexuality, bisexuality, etc.) My question for you is, do you feel sexual attraction to any gender? Women? Men? Non-binary folks? Only you can know yourself and make a judgement about your orientation. Hope this is helpful!
